tools.name: Android Debug Bridge
tools.notes: Read-only collection can be P1; install, shell, backup, restore, and file writes use A2.

tools.name: AFL++
tools.notes: Run local targets in disposable corpus/output directories with CPU, memory, time, and crash quotas.

tools.name: Aircrack-ng
tools.notes: Offline PCAP cracking is P0 and monitor capture is P1; injection and deauthentication require the A3 receipt.

tools.name: OWASP Amass
tools.notes: Passive data sources are P1; active DNS enumeration uses engagement scope and provider rate limits.

tools.name: Android Emulator
tools.license: Mixed Android Open Source Project and SDK terms
tools.notes: Use a dedicated test image with deterministic snapshots and reset; do not load personal device data.

tools.name: angr
tools.notes: Bound solver time, memory, input size, and path count.

tools.name: Apktool
tools.notes: Decode copied artifacts and preserve the original package hash.

tools.name: Arkime
tools.notes: Run as an on-demand local case service with explicit capture retention and disk quotas.

tools.name: Autopsy
tools.notes: Keep case databases private and source images read-only.

tools.name: Bandit
tools.notes: Static Python analysis with a pinned configuration and baseline.

tools.name: Bettercap
tools.notes: Passive sniffing is P1; spoofing, MITM, credential interception, and injection require the A3 receipt.

tools.name: Binwalk
tools.notes: Extract into quota-limited disposable directories and treat every extracted file as hostile.

tools.name: BloodHound Community Edition
tools.notes: Graph analysis is P0 after collection; directory collection and authenticated enumeration use the A2 gate.

tools.name: BlueZ
tools.notes: Passive discovery is P1; connecting, pairing, service interaction, and writes use A2.

tools.name: BtleJack
tools.notes: Sniffing can be P1; hijacking and jamming require the A3 receipt and compatible hardware.

tools.name: bulk_extractor
tools.license: GPL-3.0-or-later with government and third-party components
tools.notes: Use read-only evidence images and quotas for output, recursion, and workers.

tools.name: Burp Suite
tools.notes: Optional adapter only. GATE never downloads, redistributes, or accepts the Burp license; the operator supplies Community or Professional.

tools.name: capa
tools.notes: Pin the rule repository revision with every result.

tools.name: Cartography
tools.notes: Use read-only APIs and a local graph database; protect graph exports as private evidence.

tools.name: Chainsaw
tools.notes: Pin Sigma and mapping revisions with each offline event-log result.

tools.name: Checkov
tools.notes: Static IaC analysis; remote modules and external checks must be pinned.

tools.name: CloudFox
tools.notes: Enumeration only with a named account, role, regions, and local private output directory.

tools.name: Commix
tools.notes: Command-injection detection is A2; command execution and post-exploitation require the A3 receipt.

tools.name: Cutter
tools.notes: GUI front end for Rizin; dynamic debugging remains A2.

tools.name: Dalfox
tools.notes: Browser-backed XSS verification may execute target-controlled content and stays inside the A2 gate.

tools.name: DNSx
tools.notes: Restrict names and resolvers to an engagement and cap query rate.

tools.name: ExifTool
tools.notes: Operate on copied artifacts; metadata writes are disabled in the analysis adapter.

tools.name: Falco
tools.notes: Detection only by default; response hooks and automatic containment are disabled.

tools.name: Feroxbuster
tools.notes: Keep recursion same-origin and cap depth, concurrency, and total requests.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.notes: Path discovery can run as A1; body fuzzing, authenticated brute force, and high request rates use A2.

tools.name: Frida
tools.notes: Observation hooks can be P1; method replacement, bypasses, and state changes use A2. Match client and server versions exactly.

tools.name: GNU Debugger
tools.notes: Core-file analysis is P0; process attachment, calls, and memory writes use A2.

tools.name: Ghidra
tools.notes: Static analysis is P0; debugger attach, live memory access, and process control use the A2 gate.

tools.name: Gitleaks
tools.notes: Never render detected secret values into model context or normal terminal logs.

tools.name: GNU Radio
tools.notes: Offline flowgraphs are P0 and receive is P1; any transmitter block uses A2.

tools.name: Gosec
tools.notes: Static Go analysis with a pinned configuration and rule set.

tools.name: gowitness
tools.notes: Visit only approved URLs; isolate the browser and treat page content and downloads as hostile.

tools.name: Greenbone OpenVAS Scanner
tools.notes: Keep safe and intrusive checks in separate policies; use the official community container stack pinned by digest.

tools.name: Grype
tools.notes: Record vulnerability database and source artifact digests with every result.

tools.name: HackRF Tools
tools.notes: Receive is P1; transmission uses A2 and must remain within approved frequencies and power.

tools.name: Hashcat
tools.notes: Offline hashes only; recovered credentials remain in private evidence and never enter prompts or logs.

tools.name: Hayabusa
tools.notes: Pin rule revision and keep event-log evidence private.

tools.name: hcxdumptool
tools.notes: Active frame transmission and client interaction require the A3 receipt; passive capture must be explicitly configured.

tools.name: hcxtools
tools.notes: Offline conversion and analysis of authorized capture files.

tools.name: Honggfuzz
tools.notes: Remote or stateful target fuzzing is prohibited unless the A2 plan names the endpoint and recovery behavior.

tools.name: httpx
tools.notes: Run only for engagement hosts with bounded concurrency, redirects, and request rate.

tools.name: Impacket
tools.notes: Parsers are P0 and enumeration can be A1; remote execution, relay, and secret dumping require the A3 receipt.

tools.name: JADX
tools.notes: Static decompilation only; preserve the original APK hash.

tools.name: John the Ripper
tools.notes: Offline hashes only; protect pot files and recovered credentials as private evidence.

tools.name: Kali Linux compatibility toolbox
tools.notes: Optional digest-pinned compatibility image, not the source of truth. Dedicated tool entries remain authoritative and privileged containers are not a security boundary.

tools.name: Katana
tools.notes: Enforce origin scope, crawl depth, browser behavior, and a request budget.

tools.name: KillerBee
tools.notes: Zigbee sniffing is P1; replay, injection, and active interaction use A2.

tools.name: Kismet
tools.notes: Normal profile is passive monitoring with explicit interface, channel, duration, and retention limits.

tools.name: kube-bench
tools.notes: Use audit-only access and name the benchmark revision and cluster.

tools.name: kube-hunter
tools.notes: Passive discovery may be A1; active hunters and exploit validation use the A2 gate.

tools.name: kubeaudit
tools.notes: Manifest analysis is P0; live cluster audit uses a read-only service account.

tools.name: Kubescape
tools.notes: Manifest analysis is P0; live posture analysis uses a read-only service account.

tools.name: libimobiledevice
tools.notes: Device information and collection can be P1; install, restore, and write operations use A2.

tools.name: LLDB
tools.notes: Core-file analysis is P0; process attachment and mutation use A2.

tools.name: Maigret
tools.notes: Apply site rate limits and keep identity correlation evidence private.

tools.name: Manticore
tools.notes: Use offline with solver, time, and state-count bounds.

tools.name: Masscan
tools.notes: Require an explicit CIDR and conservative packet rate; never infer internet-scale scope.

tools.name: Metasploit Framework
tools.notes: Classify auxiliary modules separately. Exploit execution, payloads, and sessions always require the A3 receipt.

tools.name: mitmproxy
tools.notes: Capture-only use is P1. Request modification, upstream interception, and certificate changes use the A2 gate.

tools.name: Mobile Security Framework MobSF
tools.notes: Static analysis is P0; dynamic analysis, emulator control, and traffic interception use A2.

tools.name: Naabu
tools.notes: Enforce approved CIDRs, ports, host count, and packet rate. Raw SYN mode needs a capability broker.

tools.name: NetExec
tools.notes: Register modules separately: enumeration A1, credential spraying A2, and execution or dumping A3.

tools.name: Nikto
tools.notes: Do not vendor or separately redistribute the Nikto databases; apply host and request budgets.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.notes: NPSL is source-available and non-standard. Connect scans can be A1; raw scans and intrusive, exploit, or broadcast NSE scripts stay A2.

tools.name: Nuclei
tools.notes: Pin the template repository commit and admit signed templates by protocol and effect; code, headless, fuzz, and intrusive templates remain A2.

tools.name: Objection
tools.notes: Runtime modifications and bypasses require the A2 gate and an authorized app/device.

tools.name: osquery
tools.notes: Use a read-only SQL allowlist for P1. Extensions, event actions, and host changes use A2.

tools.name: OSV-Scanner
tools.notes: Local lockfile analysis is P0; record online database revision and query time.

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.notes: Passive or baseline operation is lower risk; active scan and authenticated scripting use the A2 gate.

tools.name: Pacu
tools.notes: Use a dedicated offensive account. Any state-changing module or credential abuse requires the A3 receipt.

tools.name: PhoneInfoga
tools.notes: Use only for a documented case purpose and protect collected personal information.

tools.name: Plaso
tools.notes: Bound parser set, image size, worker count, and output storage.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.notes: Read-only navigation can be P1. Form submission, upload, purchase, or account changes stay A2.

tools.name: Prowler
tools.notes: Use a read-only audit role by default. Remediation and fix modes use the A2 gate.

tools.name: Proxmark3
tools.notes: Offline decode is P0 and reads can be P1; emulation, writes, and credential operations use A2.

tools.name: Pwndbg
tools.notes: Pin the Pwndbg release with its supported GDB version; live target work remains A2.

tools.name: pwntools
tools.notes: Parsing and payload construction are P0; remote exploit interaction and shell handling require the A3 receipt.

tools.name: QEMU
tools.notes: Offline emulation is P0; bridged networking, KVM, USB, and host-device passthrough use A2.

tools.name: radare2
tools.notes: Static analysis is P0; live process writes and debugging use A2. Record the runtime license SBOM.

tools.name: Reverse Engineer Anything
tools.notes: Pin a tested source commit until current Wireshark, Frida, and other providers reach a stable release; retain REA provenance and effect records.

tools.name: Recon-ng
tools.notes: Admit modules individually according to source terms, effects, secrets, and rate limits.

tools.name: Responder
tools.notes: Poisoning is disabled unless the exact interface, subnet, duration, and captured-data handling are approved.

tools.name: Rizin
tools.notes: Static analysis is P0; live process changes use A2.

tools.name: rtl_433
tools.notes: Receive-only decoding; protect identifiers and household telemetry as private evidence.

tools.name: RustScan
tools.notes: Use only as a bounded discovery front end for an admitted Nmap command.

tools.name: Scapy
tools.notes: Packet decoding is P0. Sending, spoofing, replay, and protocol fuzzing use the A2 gate.

tools.name: Schemathesis
tools.notes: Generated API calls can mutate server state; allowlist operations and test identities.

tools.name: ScoutSuite
tools.notes: Use dedicated read-only cloud credentials and an API request budget.

tools.name: scrcpy
tools.notes: Viewing is P1; input injection and device control use A2.

tools.name: SearchSploit / ExploitDB
tools.notes: Searching is P0; compiling or executing a proof of concept requires the A3 receipt.

tools.name: Semgrep Community Edition
tools.notes: Use local pinned rules unless registry access and source disclosure are explicitly allowed.

tools.name: Sherlock
tools.notes: Apply site rate limits and a documented personal-data purpose and retention period.

tools.name: The Sleuth Kit
tools.notes: Analyze verified read-only image copies and record source hashes.

tools.name: Sliver
tools.notes: Engagement or lab only; pin listener addresses and record payload creation, use, revocation, and teardown.

tools.name: SpiderFoot
tools.notes: Classify modules as passive or active and retain personal data only for the stated case purpose.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.notes: Detection is A2. Extraction, filesystem access, OS command execution, and tamper scripts require the A3 receipt.

tools.name: Subfinder
tools.notes: Protect provider API keys and record which external sources were queried.

tools.name: Suricata
tools.notes: Offline IDS is P0 and live IDS is P1. Inline IPS, blocking, and NFQUEUE actions stay A2.

tools.name: Syft
tools.notes: Local SBOM generation is P0; authenticated registry reads are P1.

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.notes: Require an interface and filter, and cap duration and output size.

tools.name: testssl.sh
tools.notes: Restrict operation to engagement TLS endpoints and cap connections.

tools.name: THC Hydra
tools.notes: Credential audits require an account list, lockout policy, attempt cap, and stop-on-success behavior.

tools.name: theHarvester
tools.notes: Record source terms and API use; active DNS checks use the engagement gate.

tools.name: Timesketch
tools.notes: Run as a local case service; imports and notebooks may contain sensitive evidence.

tools.name: Trivy
tools.notes: Local files and images are P0; registries, clusters, and cloud APIs are P1. Record database revision.

tools.name: TruffleHog
tools.notes: Local scanning is P0; remote repositories and verification APIs are P1. Seal discovered values.

tools.name: TShark
tools.notes: Offline PCAP analysis is P0; live interfaces require a declared source and capture broker.

tools.name: Ubertooth
tools.notes: Receive-only capture is P1; active radio functions use A2.

tools.name: Unblob
tools.notes: Use a disposable extraction directory with file count, size, recursion, and decompression limits.

tools.name: Velociraptor
tools.notes: Read-only hunts are P1, collection is A2, and endpoint execution or remediation requires the A3 receipt.

tools.name: Volatility 3
tools.notes: VSL is a non-standard source-available license. Pin symbols and preserve the memory image hash.

tools.name: Wapiti
tools.notes: Enable only admitted non-destructive modules unless the engagement explicitly permits their effects.

tools.name: WinAFL
tools.notes: Use copied Windows targets and disposable corpus/output directories with resource limits.

tools.name: Wireshark
tools.notes: Live capture is P1 through a narrow capture broker. Prefer offline copies and disable name resolution for repeatable analysis.

tools.name: YARA
tools.notes: Pin rules by commit and preserve the matched byte evidence without exposing sensitive samples.

tools.name: Zeek
tools.notes: Offline PCAP analysis is P0; live monitoring is P1 and must preserve source timestamps.

tools.name: ZMap
tools.notes: Internet-scale operation is disabled unless the engagement names the range and rate explicitly.
